pharm: Nitrogen-containing bisphosphonate that binds hydroxyapatite at sites of active bone resorption and inhibits osteoclast activity, reducing bone turnover and increasing bone mineral density
quick: Osteoporosis treatment 70 mg once weekly (or 10 mg daily); prevention 35 mg weekly / 5 mg daily
Take on empty stomach with plain water 30 min before first food/drink/medication
Not for use in pregnancy; discontinue when pregnancy recognized
Limit - excess alcohol worsens bone loss and GI irritation
Correct hypocalcaemia/vitamin D first; dental exam; thigh/groin pain
summary: Alendronic acid (alendronate) is an oral nitrogen-containing bisphosphonate used to treat osteoporosis in postmenopausal women and to increase bone mass in men with osteoporosis (and, at lower doses, prevention and glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis). It must be taken on an empty stomach with plain water, while remaining upright (sitting or standing) for at least 30 minutes before the first food, drink or other medication, to ensure absorption and minimize esophageal injury. Hypocalcaemia and vitamin D deficiency must be corrected first. Class risks include upper GI/esophageal adverse reactions, osteonecrosis of the jaw, atypical low-trauma femoral fractures and severe musculoskeletal pain; the optimal duration is not established and a drug holiday is considered after 3-5 years in low-fracture-risk patients.
indications: Treatment of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women
Treatment to increase bone mass in men with osteoporosis
Prevention of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women (lower-dose regimen)
Treatment of glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis (per certain alendronate labeling)

dosage.d: 70 mg once weekly OR 10 mg once daily
dosage.n: Take first thing in the morning

dosage.d: 70 mg once weekly OR 10 mg once daily
35 mg once weekly OR 5 mg once daily
5 mg once daily (10 mg daily in postmenopausal women not on estrogen)

admin: Take upon arising for the day, at least 30 minutes before the first food, beverage or other medication, with a full glass of plain water (not mineral/flavored water, coffee or juice)
Do not lie down for at least 30 minutes after the dose and until after the first food of the day; do not chew or suck the tablet (oropharyngeal ulceration risk)
Correct hypocalcaemia and vitamin D deficiency before starting; ensure adequate calcium and vitamin D intake
For the effervescent (Binosto) tablet, dissolve in ~4 oz plain room-temperature water, wait until effervescence stops, stir and drink
moa: Alendronate binds preferentially to hydroxyapatite at sites of active bone resorption beneath osteoclasts. It does not impair osteoclast recruitment or attachment but inhibits osteoclast resorptive activity, reducing bone turnover; because formation then exceeds resorption at remodeling sites, bone mass progressively increases. While embedded in bone matrix it is pharmacologically inactive, so continued dosing is required.

absolute: Esophageal abnormalities that delay esophageal emptying (e.g. stricture, achalasia)
Inability to stand or sit upright for at least 30 minutes
Hypersensitivity to alendronate or any component (urticaria, angioedema reported)
relative: Increased risk of aspiration (avoid oral solution/effervescent forms)
Active upper GI disease (dysphagia, esophagitis, gastritis, ulcers, Barrett's esophagus)
Invasive dental procedures / poor dental health (ONJ risk)
monitor: Serum calcium and vitamin D status
New thigh or groin pain (atypical fracture)

preg: Available data are insufficient to assess drug-associated risk; bisphosphonates are incorporated into bone matrix and released over years. Animal data show maternal/fetal effects related to hypocalcaemia and reduced fetal ossification. Discontinue when pregnancy is recognized; alendronate is not indicated for use in women of typical childbearing intent.
lact: There are no data on the presence of alendronate in human milk; it is not indicated/recommended for use in nursing women.
renal: Not recommended in patients with creatinine clearance below 35 mL/min owing to lack of experience. No dose adjustment is needed for CrCl >=35 mL/min.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is needed for hepatic impairment (alendronate is not metabolized and is excreted renally).

moderate: Calcium supplements, antacids and oral products with multivalent cations (Ca, Mg, Al, Fe) - markedly reduce absorption; separate by at least 30 minutes (take alendronate first)
Aspirin / NSAIDs - increased risk of upper GI adverse events, especially with higher alendronate doses
minor: Levothyroxine - bioavailability of alendronate slightly decreased (clinically minor)
interactions.food: Any food or beverage other than plain water markedly reduces absorption; coffee or orange juice reduce bioavailability by ~60% - take fasting with plain water 30 min before anything else
interactions.alcohol: Excessive alcohol worsens bone loss and GI irritation - advise moderation
interactions.diagnostics: May transiently lower serum calcium and phosphate; bisphosphonates can interfere with some bone-imaging agents

serious: Esophagitis, esophageal ulcer/erosion/stricture, upper GI bleeding
rare: Osteonecrosis of the external auditory canal
emergency: Difficulty/pain on swallowing, retrosternal pain or new/worsening heartburn (esophageal injury) - stop drug
New thigh, hip or groin pain (possible atypical femoral fracture)

monitoring: Serum calcium and 25-OH vitamin D before and during therapy (correct deficiency first)
Dental examination/oral hygiene, especially before invasive dental procedures
New or worsening thigh, hip or groin pain (atypical femoral fracture)
Upper GI symptoms; reassess need for continued therapy after 3-5 years
counsel: Take first thing in the morning on an empty stomach with a full glass of plain water only, at least 30 minutes before any food, drink or other medicine
Stay sitting or standing upright for at least 30 minutes after the dose; do not chew or suck the tablet
If you get pain or difficulty swallowing, chest pain or new/worsening heartburn, stop the tablet and tell your doctor
Take calcium and vitamin D as advised, but not at the same time as alendronate
Tell your dentist you take this medicine before any dental surgery; maintain good oral hygiene
Report any new thigh, hip or groin pain
pk: Reduction in bone turnover within weeks; BMD gains over months
Oral bioavailability ~0.6%; rapidly cleared from plasma to bone or urine
Plasma terminal half-life long (>10 years) reflecting slow release from bone; plasma residence short
Prolonged - retained in bone and released over years
20-25 C (excursions 15-30 C); protect tablets from moisture; keep in original package
pearls: Strict dosing technique is essential: empty stomach, plain water only, remain upright >=30 minutes before food/other drugs - prevents esophageal injury and ensures the ~0.6% oral absorption
Correct hypocalcaemia and vitamin D deficiency BEFORE starting (contraindicated in hypocalcaemia)
Class risks: osteonecrosis of the jaw (dental clearance before invasive work) and atypical femoral fractures (evaluate new thigh/groin pain)
Optimal duration is undefined - reassess after 3-5 years and consider a drug holiday in low-fracture-risk patients
missed: For once-weekly dosing, if a dose is missed take one tablet on the morning after you remember (do not take two tablets on the same day), then return to taking one tablet on your originally chosen day. For once-daily dosing, do not take a missed dose later that day - simply resume the next morning.
overdose: Oral overdose may cause hypocalcaemia, hypophosphataemia and upper GI events (upset stomach, heartburn, esophagitis, gastritis, ulcer). Give milk or antacids to bind alendronate; because of esophageal irritation risk do NOT induce vomiting and keep the patient fully upright. Dialysis is not beneficial.
